subject: Post-demo qualification: delta accounting & 1M-token probe
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@stratascale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & proposed bench plan after today's demo

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the candid discussion about cost sensitivity and latency targets. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight benchmark plan so we can quantify the gaps you care about.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary: per-1M token economics vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (cost delta + predictable unit cost under burst).
- Secondary: p50/p95 latency constraints (target p50 < 250ms for short prompts) and cache behavior for multi-turn flows.
- Regulatory: audit log and retention expectations (30 days) — noted.

Proposed focused tests (2-week probe):
1) Baseline per-1M token comparison (Redwood hosted vs Hyperscaler A / Hyperscaler B)
   - Metric: effective $/1M tokens (including overheads: batching, network egress where applicable)
   - Data points: 1k representative requests (we'll ask for sample traffic)
2) Batching sensitivity sweep
   - Batch sizes: 1, 8, 32 (and an intermediate 12 if traffic pattern supports)
   - Capture change in p95 latency and tokens/sec; record tail amplification
3) KV/prefix cache hit-rate scenarios
   - Simulate 0%, 30%, 70% cache hit rates for multi-turn dialogs
   - Report per-token unit cost impact and latency improvements
4) Quantized model variant check (if allowed by your compliance team)
   - 8-bit vs fp16 throughput and small-quality check (BLEU/ROUGE-style pass/fail on a short eval set)

Deliverables:
- Benchmark report with tables: $/1M tokens, p50/p95 latency, failure rate, required infra assumptions (GPU types, spot vs reserved), and runbooks for getting similar outcomes in Dedicated/Private modes.
- Recommended configuration for your workload (batching settings, cache TTLs, model variant, routing policy).

What we need from you to start:
- A small, sanitized sample of traffic (1k requests) representative of typical prompt length and multi-turn ratio. Attachment: stratascale_sample_traffic_v1.json (feel free to redact PII).
- Any hyperscaler billing/discount assumptions we should model (if you want us to model your negotiated unit prices).
- Go/no-go on us running a short pilot on a dedicated pool (48–72h).

Proposed next steps:
- If you approve, we'll spin up the bench, run the tests, and aim to deliver an initial readout within 10 business days.
- I'll loop in Ben to coordinate credentialing/synthetic traffic if you prefer not to share real samples.

Thanks — GR

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

(Attachment: stratascale_sample_traffic_v1.json)

From: Anita Rao <anita@stratascale.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratascale.com
Date: 2026-08-18T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed bench plan after today's demo

Thanks Grace — that aligns with how we're thinking about evaluation. A few clarifications:

- Priority is cost first, then latency. If we can show a 20–30% unit-cost improvement at our traffic profile, we can move to a pilot.
- Latency: p50 under 250ms is important for our UI interactions; p95 < 800ms is acceptable for background flows.
- Data: we'll share a sanitized sample (1k rows) by EOD tomorrow. We need Redwood to commit to not using the raw samples for model training and to honor 30-day retention for logs.

I've looped procurement for SOW/contract work. Attaching a short SOW outline for the pilot and an internal compliance note.

Regards,
Anita
VP, Product — StrataScale
anita@stratascale.com
(Attachment: SOW_outline_StrataScale.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@stratascale.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed bench plan after today's demo

Looping in the technical bench plan and a couple implementation asks.

Ben's bench notes (high level):
- We can mirror Hyperscaler A/B using either their public API (requires creds) or a synthetic replay engine using the sample traffic. If StrataScale prefers not to share creds, synthetic replay + head-to-head costs modeling is sufficient for an apples-to-apples comparison.
- For cost math we will capture: tokenization contiguity, outbound egress (if applicable), persistent KV memory overhead (for Dedicated), and amortized GPU-hours per 1M tokens.
- We'll run three runs per configuration and report median; record CPU/GPU utilization to help explain deltas.

Immediate asks from StrataScale:
1) Confirm whether we can use synthetic replay or provide creds for Hyperscaler endpoints.
2) Provide the sanitized 1k sample and a small eval set (50 prompts) to check quality across quantized variants.

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0–2: credentialing / traffic handoff / runbook triage
- Day 3–8: bench runs (multiple configs: batching sweep, cache hit scenarios)
- Day 9–10: analysis + deliverable

Attaching the cost matrix we'll use to capture per-run deltas.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(Attachment: hyperscaler_cost_matrix.xlsx)
